A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UP-VLA study, with readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends with references despite an unresolved appendix reference; v3 supplies Appendices A–B. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.5 report original CALVIN and real-robot evaluations, component ablations, and VQA/future-prediction examples, alongside baseline results attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulation, real-robot, ablation and qualitative results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 6–7.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same backbone, continuous/discrete image encoding, scene-description conditioning, action head, two-stage training and losses. Appendix A provides implementation specificity without describing a replacement component or changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use Bridge, LLaVA-tuning-665k, CALVIN and the same Panda manipulation task categories. Appendix B elaborates existing real-world scenarios; examples such as arrow picking and small-ball manipulation already appear in v1 Figure 5.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 6 retain identical comparator memberships, including UP-VLA-RT-2 and UP-VLA-phi-w/o-mmu. Newly cited VLA papers are not added to the reported experimental comparisons.

E3.justification: The CALVIN ABC→D and ABCD→D splits, five-task evaluation and real-robot success-rate protocol remain unchanged. Appendix A newly discloses training settings rather than revising previously stated settings or establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 3 retains the same four component ablations, and Figure 7 retains the same VQA and future-image case studies. The appendices introduce no additional ablation, robustness test or error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 real-world attempts per task and retain the same point-estimate reporting. v3 adds no seed counts, repeated-training information, error bars, confidence intervals or statistical tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 match, including UP-VLA's CALVIN average lengths of 4.08 for ABC→D and 4.42 for ABCD→D. Figure 6's success rates and Figure 7's qualitative examples are also unchanged; the appendices add no results.

T1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same task definitions, prediction factorization, prompting equations and loss expressions. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The unified understanding/prediction/action contribution, claimed 33% CALVIN improvement and real-robot performance claims remain. The abstract refocuses its background wording on visual and spatial information, without changing the contributions or their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of semantic and visual generalization remain, as do the limitations concerning object-identification errors and incorrect predicted background colors. The new Impact Statement repeats the existing motivation rather than adding a substantive interpretation or limitation.

D1.justification: Previously absent Appendices A–B substantially expand reproducibility information: the Showo-512x512 (1.3B) checkpoint, MagVIT identification, 20k pretraining steps, batch size 64, 1k-step warmup, and manual versus scripted demonstration collection. v3 also adds a code-repository link. These are documentation and access-information additions, not demonstrated changes to the experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to OpenHelix, QUAR-VLA, Humanoid-VLA, VLAS, Song et al.'s parallel-decoding work and MagVIT. These extend citation coverage while retaining the existing research positioning and comparison with earlier VLA and prediction-based approaches.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged. v3 lightly edits the abstract, adds an Impact Statement and Appendices A–B, resolves the appendix cross-reference, and adds equal-contribution and publication notes.

P2.justification: The seven figures and three tables retain their content and display structure. Figure 6 moves from page 7 to page 8, and Figure 7 moves from page 8 to page 9; surrounding text and equations reflow, with additional publication and appendix layout.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies training and data-collection details missing from v1, adds a code pointer, and repairs the unresolved appendix reference. These improve transparency and reproducibility information, while the method, empirical evidence, scientific argument and stated limitations remain essentially unchanged.
